claims.claim: The agents did not necessarily know which part of a question would change from one round to the next (e.g. after R1 asked for US tobacco prevalence in 1990, whether the year, country, or metric would move).
claims.report_quote: The models didn’t necessarily know what part of the question would change from one round to the next.
spans: The models didn’t necessarily know what part of the question would change from one round to the next.
For example, after round one requested US tobacco prevalence, 1990, the agent wrote:
Likely follow-up changes year or country; timer may be very short.
claims.anchor_note: Direct statement and its immediately following US tobacco prevalence example are anchored.

claims.claim: The wiki's editors self-identify as Anthropic agents.
claims.note: Making the inference that the editors identify as Anthropic rather than just giving a quote of the name which will often say “Anthropic” is important. In this corpus the names also read “Claude”, and some misspell the maker (“Antropic”, “Antrophic”); any of these counts as self-identifying as Anthropic.
claims.report_quote: The models self-identify as Anthropic agents: They use names like “AnthropicResearcher”, “AnthropicJul3Watcher”, and “ClaudeResearchMar26”.
spans: The models self-identify as Anthropic agents: They use names like “AnthropicResearcher”, “AnthropicJul3Watcher”, and “ClaudeResearchMar26”.
claims.anchor_note: The models self-identify as Anthropic agents: They use names like “AnthropicResearcher”, “AnthropicJul3Watcher”, and “ClaudeResearchMar26”.

claims.claim: Page edits come from AWS IPs, so the agent sandboxes were hosted in AWS.
claims.note: Saying AWS is important here. The edit prefixes are 3.x, 54.x, 18.x, 44.x, 35.x and 34.x; a report that attributes them to Amazon, AWS or EC2 satisfies this, one that only lists the prefixes does not.
claims.report_quote: Page edits are from AWS IPs, meaning that agent sandboxes were hosted in AWS clusters:
spans: Of ~17,000 edits on DSEWiki that appear to be by agents, 98.5% are from Amazon Web Services IP addresses.
Page edits are from AWS IPs, meaning that agent sandboxes were hosted in AWS clusters:
claims.anchor_note: The second span directly states the claimed AWS-origin and AWS-hosting inference, while the first quantifies the AWS edits.

claims.claim: The scale of the deployment would be unusual and expensive for an actor outside an AI company.
claims.note: The claim should directly reduce the reader's probability estimate that this is an actor outside of Anthropic; just saying it is big is not enough.
claims.report_quote: This would be unusual and expensive for an actor outside an AI company to run.
spans: The scale and duration of the agent traffic are most consistent with internal model development: A large number of agents (over 3,700 distinct self-given agent names) ran across sandboxes over a six-week period. This would be unusual and expensive for an actor outside an AI company to run.
claims.anchor_note: The anchored passage links the scale and six-week duration to internal model development and explicitly characterizes an outside actor as unlikely on cost and unusualness grounds.

claims.claim: The agents were likely from an internal Anthropic deployment.
claims.report_quote: This is a “swarm” of internally deployed Anthropic agents using the internet in unintended ways.
spans: This is a “swarm” of internally deployed Anthropic agents using the internet in unintended ways.

The scale and duration of the agent traffic are most consistent with internal model development: A large number of agents (over 3,700 distinct self-given agent names) ran across sandboxes over a six-week period.
claims.anchor_note: The report directly identifies the swarm as internally deployed Anthropic agents and says its scale and duration best fit internal model development.
